description: Sixteen stage programmer modelled on the CGS sixteen step Serge programmer. One stage is selected at a time, and the four voltages programmed into it appear at the A, B, C and D outputs

params.text: Switches that stage's pulses on and off; with it off the stage sends no pulse when it is selected
Sets the voltage the A output carries while that stage is selected; the range is chosen in the menu
Sets the voltage the B output carries while that stage is selected; the range is chosen in the menu
Sets the voltage the C output carries while that stage is selected; the range is chosen in the menu
Sets the voltage the D output carries while that stage is selected; the range is chosen in the menu
Which of three things a forward step does at that stage, shown by the colour: green selects it, red stops the stepping there, grey passes over it
Which of three things a backward step does at that stage, shown by the colour: green selects it, red stops the stepping there, grey passes over it
Selects that stage by hand, and lights blue while that stage is the selected one
How many pulses that stage sends when it is selected, 1 to 8; more than one arrives as subdivisions of the step

inputs.text: A pulse here selects that stage
A pulse steps the selection forward one stage; the forward mode of each stage governs whether the stepping carries on, stops there or passes over it
A pulse steps the selection backward one stage; the backward mode of each stage governs whether the stepping carries on, stops there or passes over it
A voltage selects a stage directly, read as a note at a twelfth of a volt per stage and clipped to the sixteen stages

outputs.text: Sends a pulse each time that stage is selected, or the several set by its repetitions knob; nothing comes out while that stage's pulses are switched off
Carries the voltage programmed into the selected stage on channel A; the menu can make this four polyphonic channels carrying A, B, C and D together
Carries the voltage programmed into the selected stage on channel B
Carries the voltage programmed into the selected stage on channel C
Carries the voltage programmed into the selected stage on channel D
A pulse whenever any stage sends its pulses, so the pulses of the whole sequence arrive on one cable
A gate while a stage is selected, and while its button is held down; patch it to another Programmer to keep the two in step

menu: Preset scales — snaps the four CV outputs to one of eighteen scales, from AEOLIAN to TURKISH; NO QUANTIZER, the default, passes the knob voltages as they are
From 0V to 10V, From -5V to 5V, From 0V to 5V, From -2.5V to 2.5V, From 0V to 2V, From -1V to 1V and From 0V to 1V — each sets the range of the four CV outputs
ADDR: pulse out when stage change — makes a stage picked by the ADDR voltage send its pulses, which selecting by ADDR does not otherwise do
Use PULSE > and/or PULSE < signals to sample incoming ADDR CV — reads the ADDR voltage only when a pulse arrives at > or <, rather than following it continuously
Channel A, TRIG and PUSH are poly 4 channel — turns those three outputs into four channel polyphonic outputs, A then carrying the four channel voltages
Copy TRACK 1 — copies the sixteen voltages of track 1 over another track, chosen from to 2, to 3 and to 4; Copy TRACK 2, Copy TRACK 3 and Copy TRACK 4 do the same for the other tracks
Nudge Forward — shifts one track's sixteen programmed voltages one stage forward, the track chosen from Track 1, Track 2, Track 3 and Track 4
Nudge Backward — shifts one track's sixteen programmed voltages one stage backward, the track chosen from Track 1, Track 2, Track 3 and Track 4
